International Society for Krishna Consciousness
------------------------------------------
Abbreviated as ISKCON, this is a recent Hindu Religious movement started by Bhaktivedanta Swami Prabhupada (A. D. 1896-1977) in A. D. 1966 in the United States of America (at New York). Known as Abhay Charan De in his premonastic days, he met his गुरु Bhaktisiddhanta Thakur in A. D. 1922 at Kolkata and received spiritual initiation from him in A. D. 1932. Being spiritually inclined and fed up with family life he accepted the monastic vows in A. D. 1959 at वृन्दाबन् (in Uttar Pradesh). Henceforward he came to be known as Bhaktivedānta Svāmi Prabhupāda, but more commonly as Śrīla Prabhupāda.
He has many books to his credit, the translations of the Bhagavadgītā and the Bhāgavata being his best works.
He was responsible in building a magnificent temple of कृष्ण-बलराम at वृन्दाबन् and a holy city called Māyāpur in West Bengal.
When he started the ISKCON movement he kept before it seven ideals. Some of them are: to systematically propagate spiritual knowledge to the society at large; to spread the idea that कृष्ण is the God as revealed in the Bhagavadgītā and the Bhāgavata; to teach and encourage the saṅkīrtana movement (community singing of bhajans); to publish books and periodicals on the theme and philosophy of the movement.
This whole movement is based on the life and message of श्रीकृष्ण चैतन्य (A. D. 1486-1533) and the Gauḍīya Vaiṣṇava tradition of Bengal.
Because of the great stress laid on the repetition of the famous मन्त्र hare कृष्ण hare कृष्ण kṛṣṇa कृष्ण hare hare; hare राम hare राम rāma राम hare hare (Kalisantaraṇa Upaniṣad-1), The organisation has come to be known as “The Hare Krishna Movement”.
Devotees wanting to accept formal initiation into the chanting of this holy मन्त्र are expected to observe certain vows like abstaining from drinking, गम्ब्लिन्ग्, eating meat and illicit sexual relationships.
The movement claims to have 350 centres spread all over the world. Apart from huge temples dedicated to कृष्ण, the movement sometimes undertakes social welfare programmes also.
There is a Governing Body Commission (GBC) formed in A. D. 1970 to guide the organisation.
The Bhaktivedanta Book Trust (BBT) established in A. D. 1972 has brought out several volumes of the founder’s books over the last few years as also magazines in several languages.
